subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Lie, Attitude, Presentation, Position and Denominator

steps.tx: The relation of the fetal long axis to the mothers long axis is the **lie**. Longitudinal lie is normal, transverse and oblique lies are abnormal near term. Lie is described before presentation in every examination. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Lie relates the fetal axis to the mothers, with longitudinal being normal.

steps.tx: The posture of fetal parts to each other, usually full flexion, is the **attitude**. A flexed attitude presents the smallest diameters to the pelvis. Deflexion and extension produce brow and face presentations. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Attitude describes fetal flexion, with full flexion presenting the smallest diameters.

steps.tx: The fetal part first entering the pelvis and felt vaginally is the **presentation**. Vertex presentation of the flexed head is by far the commonest. Breech, face, brow and shoulder presentations each carry distinct risks. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Presentation is the part entering the pelvis first, with vertex being commonest.

steps.tx: The relation of a chosen point on the presentation to the mothers pelvis is the **position**. Left occipitotransverse and similar terms locate the denominator precisely. Position determines the rotation needed for birth. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Position relates the denominator to the mothers pelvis and determines rotation needed.

steps.tx: The reference point on the presenting part used to describe position is the **denominator**. Occiput for vertex, sacrum for breech and mentum for face are standard. Every position statement is meaningless without its denominator. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: The denominator is the reference point making every position statement meaningful.

steps.tx: Descent level relative to the ischial spines measured in centimetres is the **station**. Zero station sits at the spines, negative above and positive below. Station complements abdominal fifths in judging progress. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Station measures descent against the ischial spines in centimetres above or below.

steps.tx: Compound presentation, a hand beside the head, complicates delivery and is called **compound presentation**. It often resolves as labour advances and the hand withdraws. Persistence with cord prolapse risk changes management. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Compound presentation puts a hand beside the head and often resolves as labour advances.

steps.tx: Unstable lie changing between examinations near term is **unstable lie**. Causes include polyhydramnios, placenta praevia and pelvic tumours. Admission and stabilising induction or caesarean prevent cord accidents. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Unstable lie near term needs admission because cord accidents can follow membrane rupture.

steps.tx: Systematic description order prevents confusion and is taught as **lie presentation position**. Examiners state each element before giving an opinion on progress. Leopold manoeuvres plus vaginal findings together build the full picture. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Stating lie, presentation and position systematically prevents confusion in labour assessment.
